title: SAT Reading & Writing Practice Test 3
instructions: Each question has a short passage. Choose the best answer. Questions cover reading comprehension, vocabulary, grammar and rhetoric.

passages.title: Artificial Intelligence
passages.text: Artificial intelligence systems trained on large datasets sometimes learn patterns that reflect societal biases present in the data. When facial recognition algorithms are trained primarily on lighter-skinned faces, they perform poorly on darker-skinned individuals. This phenomenon, known as algorithmic bias, demonstrates that technology is not neutral but rather encodes the prejudices of its creators and training data.

passages.title: Cryptocurrency
passages.text: Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies operate on blockchain technology, which records transactions in a distributed ledger secured through cryptographic methods. Proponents argue that cryptocurrencies enable financial inclusion for unbanked populations and reduce intermediaries in financial transactions. Critics contend that cryptocurrency volatility, environmental costs, and association with illegal activity outweigh potential benefits.

passages.title: Vaccine Development
passages.text: The mRNA vaccine platform, demonstrated successfully against COVID-19, represents a paradigm shift in vaccine development. Rather than cultivating weakened viruses, mRNA vaccines instruct cells to produce specific viral proteins, triggering immune response. This approach enables faster development cycles compared to traditional vaccine methods, though long-term safety requires continued monitoring.

passages.title: Economic Inequality
passages.text: Economic inequality has reached historic levels in developed nations, with wealth concentrated among a small percentage of the population. Research links high inequality to reduced social mobility, worse health outcomes, and decreased economic growth. Economists debate whether inequality is inevitable in market economies or whether policy interventions can effectively redistribute resources.

passages.title: 5G Technology
passages.text: Fifth-generation mobile networks promises faster speeds and lower latency than 4G technology. 5G infrastructure requirements differ substantially from previous generations, demanding investment in new hardware and frequency bands. The technology enables applications including autonomous vehicles and real-time remote surgery.

passages.title: Healthcare Access
passages.text: Healthcare systems worldwide struggle with providing equitable access while controlling costs. Rural populations often lack proximity to medical facilities and specialists, creating disparities in health outcomes. Telemedicine technologies have potential to bridge these gaps, though digital literacy and internet access remain barriers.

passages.title: Cybersecurity Threats
passages.text: Cyberattacks on critical infrastructure have increased in frequency and sophistication, targeting power grids, water systems, and healthcare networks. Nation-states and criminal organizations exploit vulnerabilities to extort money or disrupt essential services. Improving cybersecurity requires investment in both defensive technology and workforce development.

passages.title: Mental Health Economics
passages.text: Mental health conditions costs societies billions in lost productivity and healthcare spending. Despite prevalence, mental health services remains underfunded relative to physical healthcare in many regions. Addressing mental health requires integrated approaches combining therapy, medication, and social support.

passages.title: Plastic Waste
passages.text: Single-use plastics, convenient for consumers and manufacturers, have created an environmental crisis as vast quantities accumulate in landfills and oceans. Microplastics contaminate food chains and drinking water supplies, with unknown health effects. Addressing plastic pollution requires change in production practices, consumer behavior, and policy enforcement.

passages.title: Artificial Organs
passages.text: Bioengineers are developing artificial organs to address the shortage of donor organs for transplantation. Using 3D printing and decellularized tissue scaffolds, researchers have created functional prototypes of kidneys, hearts, and livers. Clinical trials remain years away, but artificial organs could revolutionize transplantation medicine.

passages.title: Social Media Algorithms
passages.text: Social media algorithms optimize for engagement, often amplifying sensational and polarizing content that keeps users on platforms longer. This design choice has contributed to misinformation spread and deepening political polarization. Reforming these algorithms to prioritize accuracy and reduced polarization remains technically and commercially challenging.

passages.title: Pandemic Preparedness Grammar
passages.text: Pandemic preparedness involves investment in surveillance systems, vaccine manufacturing capacity, and trained personnel. The COVID-19 crisis revealed gaps in global preparedness despite previous warnings. Future pandemic prevention requires sustained political commitment and funding.

passages.title: Gene Therapy
passages.text: Gene therapy, delivering functional genes to patients to treat genetic disorders, has shown remarkable success in clinical trials. The technique offers potential cures for previously untreatable conditions including sickle cell disease and certain forms of blindness. Regulatory frameworks and manufacturing challenges remain obstacles to widespread adoption.

passages.title: Data Privacy Grammar
passages.text: Data privacy concerns intensifies as companies collects increasingly detailed personal information. Regulations like GDPR and CCPA attempt to limit data collection and grant individuals rights over their information.

passages.title: Automation and Labor
passages.text: Automation increasingly displaces workers from manufacturing and service industries, creating economic challenges for affected communities. While technology historically created new job categories, the pace of current automation exceeds workforce retraining capacity. Income inequality may widen absent policy interventions supporting displaced workers.

passages.title: Microbiome Research
passages.text: The human microbiome—trillions of bacteria and other microorganisms living in our bodies—plays crucial roles in digestion, immune function, and even mental health. Dysbiosis, imbalance in microbial communities, correlates with obesity, inflammatory bowel disease, and other conditions. Microbiome-targeted therapeutics represent an emerging frontier in personalized medicine.

passages.title: Carbon Pricing
passages.text: Carbon pricing mechanisms, either through carbon taxes or cap-and-trade systems, aim to internalize the environmental costs of greenhouse gas emissions into market prices. Economists generally support carbon pricing as efficient policy, though implementation varies globally. Carbon taxes are politically contentious because they raise energy costs for consumers.

passages.title: Neurotechnology Ethics
passages.text: Emerging neurotechnologies enables direct communication between brains and computers through brain-computer interfaces. These technologies offer promise for paralyzed individuals but raise privacy and autonomy concerns. Ethical frameworks for neurotechnology remain underdeveloped despite rapid technological advancement.

passages.title: Gig Economy Workers
passages.text: Gig economy workers often lack employment benefits including health insurance and retirement contributions, instead bearing these costs individually. Classification of gig workers as independent contractors rather than employees affects whether labor protections apply. Regulatory approaches differ globally, from protections in Europe to minimal regulation in the United States.

passages.title: Antibiotic Resistance
passages.text: Antibiotic resistance develops when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive antibiotic exposure, rendering medicines ineffective. Overuse of antibiotics in human medicine and industrial agriculture accelerates this process. Resistance to multiple antibiotics threatens to create untreatable infections, potentially reversing decades of medical progress.

passages.title: Quantum Computing
passages.text: Quantum computers exploit quantum mechanical properties to perform calculations impossible for classical computers. While still largely experimental, quantum computers could revolutionize drug discovery, cryptography, and optimization problems. Current limitations include error rates and the difficulty of maintaining quantum coherence.

passages.title: Depression Treatment Grammar
passages.text: Depression affects hundreds of millions of people globally and ranks among the leading causes of disability worldwide. Treatment approaches includes medication, therapy, lifestyle changes, and for severe cases, electroconvulsive therapy.

passages.title: Blockchain Technology
passages.text: Beyond cryptocurrency, blockchain technology has potential applications in supply chain transparency, medical records management, and voting systems. The immutable distributed ledger creates permanent records that cannot be retroactively altered without consensus. Challenges include scalability, energy consumption, and regulatory uncertainty.

passages.title: Sleep and Cognition
passages.text: Sleep deprivation impairs cognitive function including memory consolidation, attention, and decision-making. While humans can survive weeks without food, extended sleep deprivation becomes fatal. Understanding sleep's neurological basis has led to treatments for insomnia and other sleep disorders.

passages.title: Renewable Energy Storage Grammar
passages.text: Renewable energy sources like wind and solar faces the challenge of intermittency—they generate power inconsistently. Battery storage technologies must improve significantly to enable grid-scale renewable energy deployment.

passages.title: Precision Medicine
passages.text: Precision medicine tailors treatment to individual patient characteristics including genetics, lifestyle, and disease biomarkers. This approach contrasts with conventional medicine's one-size-fits-all treatment protocols. Genomic data and artificial intelligence enable increasingly sophisticated personalization.

passages.title: Digital Divide
passages.text: The digital divide separates populations with internet access and digital literacy from those without, creating disparities in education, employment, and access to services. COVID-19 pandemic highlighted this divide as schools transitioned to remote learning. Bridging the divide requires infrastructure investment and digital education initiatives.

passages.title: Longevity Research Grammar
passages.text: Aging populations in developed nations creates economic pressure on healthcare and social security systems. Longevity research investigates mechanisms of aging with goals of extending healthspan—years lived in good health.

passages.title: Food Security
passages.text: Climate change threatens global food security through crop failures, water scarcity, and disruption of agricultural systems. Population growth and dietary shifts toward meat consumption further strain food systems. Alternative proteins including plant-based and cultured meat may prove necessary to feed humanity sustainably.

passages.title: CRISPR Gene Editing
passages.text: CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technology enables precise modifications to DNA sequences, raising possibilities for treating genetic diseases and enhancing human traits. The technology's accessibility and low cost have democratized genetic research. Ethical concerns about heritable modifications and designer babies persist despite technical capability.

passages.title: Labor Market Disruption Grammar
passages.text: Technological change disrupts labor markets by displacing some workers while creating opportunities in emerging fields. Workers with technical skills benefits disproportionately from these shifts.

passages.title: Orphan Diseases
passages.text: Orphan diseases, conditions affecting very small patient populations, receive limited research funding and drug development because they lack commercial viability. Patients with rare genetic diseases often struggle to obtain diagnoses and treatment. Policy incentives like tax credits and market exclusivity have increased orphan drug development.

passages.title: Synthetic Biology
passages.text: Synthetic biology engineers biological systems to create new functions not found in nature. Applications include producing biofuels, manufacturing medicines, and creating environmental bioremediation organisms. The field raises biosafety and biosecurity concerns about unintended ecological consequences.

passages.title: Economic Stimulus Policy Grammar
passages.text: Government stimulus spending can stimulate economic growth during recessions but risks inflation if poorly timed. Economists debates whether fiscal stimulus or monetary policy proves more effective.

passages.title: Zoonotic Diseases
passages.text: Zoonotic diseases jump from animals to humans, causing outbreaks including COVID-19, Ebola, and avian influenza. Increasing contact between humans and wildlife through deforestation and industrial agriculture amplifies transmission risk. Pandemic prevention requires addressing the interfaces where animals and humans interact.

passages.title: Cryptocurrency Volatility Grammar
passages.text: Bitcoin prices fluctuate dramatically in response to market sentiment and regulatory announcements. Such volatility limits cryptocurrencies' usefulness as stable stores of value or mediums of exchange.

passages.title: Cancer Immunotherapy
passages.text: Cancer immunotherapy leverages the immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells. Checkpoint inhibitors, which remove brakes on immune function, have proven effective against multiple cancer types. Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment outcomes though resistance and side effects limit its applicability.

passages.title: Supply Chain Resilience Grammar
passages.text: Recent disruptions to global supply chains demonstrates the vulnerability of just-in-time manufacturing models. Companies increasingly prioritize resilience over pure efficiency in sourcing strategies.

passages.title: Digital Mental Health
passages.text: Digital mental health interventions including apps, chatbots, and online therapy platforms expand access to treatment. These tools offer anonymity and convenience but lack human connection and cannot adequately replace traditional therapy. Digital-enhanced care combining technology with human providers shows promise.

passages.title: Universal Basic Income
passages.text: Universal basic income proposals suggest governments provide all citizens with unconditional periodic cash payments. Proponents argue UBI could reduce poverty and provide security amid automation-driven job displacement. Critics contend that UBI is economically unsustainable and would reduce work incentives.

passages.title: Bioethics Regulation Grammar
passages.text: International bioethics frameworks attempts to establish ethical standards for emerging biotechnologies. However, implementation remains inconsistent across jurisdictions with different cultural values.

passages.title: Metabolic Syndrome
passages.text: Metabolic syndrome, a cluster of conditions including obesity, high blood pressure, and insulin resistance, increases risk for heart disease and diabetes. The syndrome reflects both individual behaviors and structural factors including food environment and sedentary lifestyles. Addressing metabolic syndrome requires interventions at multiple levels from individual to policy.

passages.title: Bioaccumulation
passages.text: Bioaccumulation occurs when toxins concentrate in organisms over time, with levels intensifying up the food chain. Persistent organic pollutants including DDT and PCBs bioaccumulate despite being banned, remaining in ecosystems for decades. This phenomenon means small environmental concentrations can create large health risks in apex predators and humans.

passages.title: Tech Work-Life Balance Grammar
passages.text: Tech industry workers often faces unrealistic deadline pressures and always-on work cultures. Company policies promising flexibility sometimes mask expectations for constant availability.

passages.title: Diabetic Complications
passages.text: Diabetes complications including retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy result from prolonged high blood glucose damaging small blood vessels and nerves. Prevention through glucose control and early detection through screening programs dramatically reduce complication rates. Management of diabetes complications requires multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

passages.title: Space Debris Grammar
passages.text: Space debris from defunct satellites and rocket stages orbits Earth at velocities exceeding 20,000 kilometers per hour. Collisions with debris endangers operational satellites and space stations, creating cascading collision events.

passages.title: Healthcare AI
passages.text: Artificial intelligence systems diagnose diseases from medical images with accuracy rivaling or exceeding human radiologists. AI algorithms can identify patterns in patient data to predict adverse outcomes and personalize treatment plans. Integration into clinical workflows faces obstacles including liability questions and need for validation across diverse populations.

passages.title: Carbon Sequestration Grammar
passages.text: Carbon sequestration technologies captures carbon dioxide from air or industrial sources and stores it permanently. Direct air capture remains technologically feasible but economically expensive currently.

passages.title: Fertility Preservation
passages.text: Fertility preservation technologies including egg and sperm freezing enable people to delay childbearing while maintaining reproductive options. Cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy or radiation often preserve fertility before treatment. Societal shifts toward delayed parenthood have increased demand for fertility preservation services.

passages.title: Trade Policy Economics Grammar
passages.text: Trade policies including tariffs and quotas affects consumer prices and business investment decisions. Economists generally supports free trade while acknowledging unequal distribution of trade gains.

passages.title: Migraine Biology
passages.text: Migraines result from complex neurobiological processes involving pain pathway sensitivity and vascular changes. Understanding migraine mechanisms has enabled development of novel preventive treatments. Migraine research illustrates how basic neuroscience discoveries translate into clinical advances.

passages.title: Labor Union Decline Grammar
passages.text: Union membership in private sector declines steadily in developed economies, shifting power dynamics in labor markets. Declining bargaining power correlates with stagnant wages and widening income inequality.

passages.title: Occupational Health
passages.text: Occupational hazards from chemical exposure, repetitive strain, and physical demands create health risks for workers. Developing countries often have minimal occupational health protections, leading to higher disease and injury rates. Ensuring workplace safety requires regulation, enforcement, and worker education.

passages.title: Economic Growth Models Grammar
passages.text: Economic growth models attempts to predict future output based on capital investment and productivity improvements. However, models often underestimates the role of technological innovation in driving growth.

questions.explanation: The passage illustrates how bias in training data creates biased technology output, concluding that technology encodes prejudices rather than being neutral.

questions.explanation: The passage cites research linking inequality to negative outcomes (reduced mobility, worse health, decreased growth) to support its main claim about inequality's harms.
